newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate rises to 11.6 vs 10.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate rises to 11.6 vs 10.6 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate rose a whole percentage point to 11.6 percent on Monday amid higher demand for term funds.

Dealers put trade at 28.1 million kuna against demand for 40 million and supply of 35 million. Fresh borrowings accounted for some 13 million kuna but some creditors and lenders failed to agree on terms for the new loans.
Most interbank prices were steady at between 11 percent for call money and 17 percent for 60-day loans. But banks charged a higher 14 percent rate for two-week kuna instead of last week's 13 percent.
Insurers rolled over almost 11 million kuna in seven-day funds at an unchanged 9.0 percent.
The kuna midrates for Tuesday firmed slightly to 6.0305 against the dollar but eased to 3.5718 agains the German mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
